psyPatient.definition: Personality: patient, plays the long game. YES when the ability's main payoff only comes after waiting, and the character's own Tips & Tricks favour waiting: a once-per-game action best saved (Slayer, Artist, Seamstress, Assassin, Judge...), a payoff on a later death or condition (Ravenkeeper, Sage, Choirboy, Banshee, Mayor, Scarlet Woman, Mastermind), a fixed later night or day (Summoner, Xaan, Riot, Leviathan), or a choice to hold back (Po, Zombuul). NO when the ability pays out from the start or every night or day with an immediate effect, leaving nothing to save up (start-knowing info, nightly info that is useful on its own, nightly kills and poisons, day-1-only or night-1-only actions). Borderline: once-per-game abilities the wiki says to use early or late depending on the game (Engineer, Nightwatchman, Courtier, Philosopher), conditional repeatable effects (Godfather, King, Pixie, Alsaahir), nightly info that only pays off once accumulated (Fortune Teller, Balloonist, Oracle), always-on passives (Soldier, Tea Lady, Magician, Pacifist, Poppy Grower, Zealot, Snitch, Boffin, Beggar), believed or borrowed abilities, and characters whose waiting is incidental.

psyRiskTaker.definition: Personality: risk-taker. YES when the ability makes the player stake their own life, their exposure or their team's win on an uncertain call they choose to make, for a payoff (Gambler, Acrobat, Exorcist, Nightwatchman, Gossip, Ogre, Golem, Puzzlemaster, Wizard, Goblin, Harlot). NO when using the ability is safe for the player, or the ability is passive with nothing the player chooses to stake (good private info, protection, passive outsider liabilities, vote modifiers). Borderline: public but downside-free actions (Slayer, Alsaahir, Juggler), forced death triggers with no payoff (Klutz, Moonchild), Po's skipped kill, and every Minion and Demon (bluffing is risky for all of them, whatever the ability).

psyNeedsControl.definition: Personality: likes to be in charge. YES when the ability lets the player dictate rules or decisions for other players: who may act or use an ability (Preacher, Courtier, Witch), how votes count or who votes or nominates (Organ Grinder, Bishop, Voudon), who is executed (Judge, Vizier), where people sit (Matron), what others must claim (Cerenovus, Harpy), or which characters exist (Pit-Hag, Engineer, Summoner, Kazali). NO when the ability is passive, merely receives information, or puts the player at the mercy of others or the Storyteller (Butler, Zealot, Atheist, info roles, passive Minions like Baron or Spy). Borderline: plain killers, protectors, unilateral strikes (Slayer, Golem), single-vote modifiers (Thief, Bureaucrat), and borrowed or believed abilities (Drunk, Marionette, Lunatic, Amnesiac).

psyShowman.definition: Personality: loves the spotlight. YES when the ability is used in public and the character plays openly: public statements, guesses, kills or choices (Gossip, Juggler, Slayer, Cult Leader, Psychopath, Goblin, Gunslinger, Gangster), being publicly known (Vizier), spectacle (Boomdandy, Riot), or performing (Deviant). NO when the ability is entirely private and works best if nobody notices the player (most Minions and night-killing Demons, Spy, Mutant, Damsel, Magician, Choirboy). Borderline: good info roles and protectors; characters that hide until one public moment (Alsaahir, Banshee, Golem, Klutz, Moonchild); hidden-in-plain-sight public effects (Yaggababble); madness (Pixie); believed abilities; and evil characters only known to be in play (Leviathan, Al-Hadikhia, Fearmonger).

psyDeceiver.definition: Personality: enjoys bluffing. YES when playing the character well means lying about who you are: every Minion and Demon that knows it is evil (except the publicly known Vizier, the Goblin who claims openly, and the Psychopath whose kills are public), plus good characters that must pretend (Pixie's madness, Mutant, Damsel). NO for good characters whose ability rewards honesty. Borderline: Travellers (alignment assigned); characters who believe they are something else (Marionette, Lunatic, Drunk) or may hold the Mutant ability (Hermit); alignment-shifters (Goon); and good characters whose wiki tips recommend bluffing to bait the Demon (Soldier, Sage, Ravenkeeper, Banshee, Farmer, Fool, Mayor, Choirboy, Lycanthrope), and the Atheist (in its game the Storyteller is breaking the rules and the table is all good).

psyManipulator.definition: Personality: pulls strings behind the scenes. YES when the ability's purpose is to secretly tamper with what other players know or can do without them choosing it: drunkenness, poison, madness, false information or hidden character and alignment changes (Poisoner, Pukka, No Dashii, Vigormortis, Widow, Xaan, Vortox, Lleech, Sailor, Courtier, Magician, Mezepheles, Cerenovus, Harpy, Pit-Hag, Witch, Cacklejack). NO when the ability never affects anyone else's information or abilities (pure info roles, plain killers, protectors, passive self-only outsiders). Borderline: drunkenness as a side cost (Innkeeper, Philosopher), indirect or public effects (Minstrel, Preacher, Engineer, Goon, Sweetheart, Poppy Grower, Kazali, Snake Charmer), secret vote tampering (Thief, Bureaucrat, Organ Grinder), hidden empowering or setup (Boffin, Baron), the Heretic's secret inversion, and believed abilities.

psySelfless.definition: Personality: puts others first. YES when the ability's main value goes to other players, at no gain or at a cost to the player: protecting others the player cannot protect themselves with (Monk, Tea Lady, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate), exposing or sacrificing yourself for the team (Exorcist, Nightwatchman, Scapegoat, Goblin), reviving or empowering others (Professor, Bone Collector, Boffin, Gnome). NO when the ability is built around the player's own survival or personal victory (Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Mayor, Politician, Zombuul, Vizier, Deviant, Lleech, Psychopath). Borderline: info roles, plain killers, death triggers (Farmer), protectors who can choose themselves (Innkeeper), team-play abilities without a cost (Princess, Summoner), the Scarlet Woman (her payoff is her own promotion but she protects the Demon), and the Goon.

psyCurious.definition: Personality: curious, needs to know. YES when the ability's main purpose is learning hidden information (every Townsfolk info role, Fisherman, Juggler, Ravenkeeper, Sage, Choirboy, Spy, Widow, Wraith, Harlot). NO when the ability never gives the player any information. Borderline: abilities where information is a side effect, a common use, or depends on borrowing (Gambler, Acrobat, Exorcist, Amnesiac, Pixie, Godfather, Evil Twin, Boffin, Puzzlemaster, Beggar, Barista, Philosopher, Cannibal, Alchemist, Hermit, Apprentice, Snake Charmer, Gossip, Slayer, Virgin, Golem, Wizard), and believed abilities.

psyIntuitive.definition: Personality: trusts the gut. YES when the ability asks the player to commit to a guess, usually early or often, that the ability gives them no evidence for (Gambler, Juggler, Amnesiac, Preacher, Snake Charmer, Exorcist, Gossip, Ogre, Ojo). NO when the ability simply hands the player facts or works without any judgement (start-knowing and nightly info roles, passives, evil characters with full knowledge of their team). Borderline: killers choosing victims and other free choices (Monk, Innkeeper, Sailor, Butler, Harlot), and decisive single guesses players are advised to back with evidence (Slayer, Golem, Alsaahir, Klutz, Moonchild, Puzzlemaster, Courtier, Huntsman).

psyPuzzler.definition: Personality: loves logic puzzles. Applies to information roles only. YES when the information arrives as a puzzle that needs deduction: one-of-several, counts, true-and-false mixes or partial clues (Chef, Empath, Investigator, Washerwoman, Librarian, Knight, Noble, Clockmaker, Shugenja, Balloonist, Chambermaid, Mathematician, Dreamer, Fortune Teller, Flowergirl, Town Crier, Oracle, Savant, Seamstress, Juggler, Sage, Amnesiac, Puzzlemaster). NO when the information is a direct answer (Steward, Grandmother, Bounty Hunter, Pixie, King, Undertaker, Artist, Ravenkeeper, Choirboy, Spy, Widow). Borderline: the Fisherman (the Storyteller's advice may be cryptic) and characters without information abilities.

psyProtective.definition: Personality: protective. YES when the ability keeps someone else alive or safe (Monk, Innkeeper, Tea Lady, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate, Exorcist, Professor, Scapegoat, Gnome). NO when the ability harms or kills others, or protects only the player themselves (killers, poisoners and madness-makers, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Mayor, Zombuul). Borderline: info roles, passive outsiders, Minions that neither harm nor protect (Baron, Mastermind, Scarlet Woman), and indirect team protection (Huntsman, Princess).

psyChaosLover.definition: Personality: loves chaos. YES when the ability makes the game less predictable for everyone: it changes characters or alignments, causes random or mass deaths, inverts or breaks the rules, or scrambles votes and seats (Pit-Hag, Cacklejack, Barber, Hatter, Atheist, Heretic, Tinker, Plague Doctor, Gossip, Harpy, Mezepheles, Wizard, Xaan, Boomdandy, Organ Grinder, Shabaloth, Kazali, Vortox, Legion, Al-Hadikhia, Riot, Thief, Matron, Voudon). NO when the ability brings order or certainty: reliable info, protection, steady passive effects, plain killing (info roles, Monk, Soldier, Mayor, Virgin, Fool, Tea Lady, Imp, Spy, Baron, Scarlet Woman). Borderline: everything in between, including demon-hunters whose swap is a side effect (Snake Charmer), the Goon, the Summoner and the No Dashii.

psyLoyal.definition: Personality: loyal. YES when the ability ties the player to one particular other player they stand by or serve (Butler, Grandmother, Choirboy, Boffin, Gnome). NO when the player's allegiance shifts or the ability serves only themselves (Politician, Goon, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Zombuul). Borderline: everyone else, including positional or whole-team ties (Tea Lady, Scapegoat, Mastermind, Lil' Monsta), the Scarlet Woman, the Lleech's parasitic tie, attaching to a stranger (Ogre), and alignment changers who still serve a group (Snake Charmer, Cult Leader, Heretic).

psyVengeful.definition: Personality: pays back wrongs. YES when the ability strikes back in response to something done to the player or their side: their death (Sage, Banshee, Choirboy for the King, Mastermind for the Demon), their nomination (Virgin), nominating or voting (Gunslinger, Gnome), an Outsider's death (Godfather) or their execution (Boomdandy). NO when the ability is purely defensive or forgiving (Monk, Innkeeper, Tea Lady, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate, Exorcist, Professor). Borderline: everyone else, including the Witch (her curse is pre-emptive) and the Moonchild (a good Moonchild's curse can only hurt good players).

psyRuthless.definition: Personality: ruthless. YES when the character's own ability lets the player choose to kill: every Demon except the Leviathan, plus the Assassin, Godfather, Psychopath, Witch, Boomdandy, Slayer, Lycanthrope, Golem, Gunslinger, Gangster and Gnome. NO when the ability never causes anyone's death. Borderline: borrowed or believed abilities that might kill, extra executions (Butcher, Virgin, Judge, Vizier, Princess), side-effect or Storyteller-chosen deaths (Pit-Hag, Harlot, Wizard, Harpy, Gossip), and the Moonchild (a good Moonchild's curse only kills good players).

psyPersuader.definition: Personality: persuader. YES when the ability only works if the player talks others into something: agreeing, saying a word, voting or executing their way, joining them, or believing their claim (Cult Leader, Mezepheles, Goblin, Mutant, Pixie, Evil Twin, Princess, Fearmonger, Vizier, Mastermind, Boomdandy, Harlot, Gangster, Beggar). NO when the ability works silently whatever anyone believes (night info, night kills, poison, protection, passives). Borderline: Gossip, Saint, Politician, Leviathan, Yaggababble, Deviant, Riot and others whose success leans on the table's mood, plus win conditions that need the town talked into or out of executing (Mayor, Atheist, Heretic, Vortox, Legion, Al-Hadikhia).

psyUnderdog.definition: Personality: happy to be underestimated. YES when the ability looks harmless or stays invisible, then matters at a key moment, often after the player is overlooked or killed (Fool, Magician, Poppy Grower, Farmer, Minstrel, Ravenkeeper, Sage, Choirboy, Banshee, Golem, Scarlet Woman, Mastermind, Zombuul). NO when the ability is loud, public or powerful from the outset (Juggler, Gossip, Cult Leader, Psychopath, Fearmonger, Vizier, Al-Hadikhia, and the public Travellers). Borderline: everyone else, including hidden one-shots (Slayer, Alsaahir), evil that lies low until a fixed moment (Riot, Leviathan, Yaggababble), and characters the wiki advises to claim openly (Soldier, Mayor, Virgin).

psyImproviser.definition: Personality: improviser. YES when the ability is open-ended and the player decides what form it takes (choosing an ability, character, wish, question or statement): Philosopher, Engineer, Artist, Gossip, Wizard, Pit-Hag, Summoner, Kazali, Bone Collector. NO when the ability has a single fixed function that works the same way every time. Borderline: abilities picked by the Storyteller or by circumstance (Cannibal, Amnesiac, Hermit, Apprentice, Alchemist), partly flexible ones (Pixie, Courtier, Ojo, Cerenovus, Boffin, Barista), improvised comedy (Deviant), and believed abilities.

psyContrarian.definition: Personality: contrarian. YES when the ability is about going against the consensus (the Devil's Advocate saves the condemned, the Heretic inverts the win, the Atheist insists there is no evil). NO when the ability makes the player go along with others (Zealot, Butler, Cult Leader, Goon, Ogre). Borderline: everyone else, including characters that merely subvert a rule without arguing against anyone (Thief, Lycanthrope, Magician, Vortox).
